summary: Most round-4 functionality is present and the claimed commands pass, but the saved-player loader still misses a core acceptance criterion: the full visible row is not actually selectable, and the narrow-width CSS regresses the new one-line row UX into stacked multi-line rows.
strengths: `npm test` passed across all 8 test files, including the updated app-flow and layout checks.
`npm run build` succeeded and produced a static `dist/` bundle suitable for frontend-only deployment.

Core round-3/round-4 behaviors appear intact from code and test inspection: header/headerless parsing, 6 candidate generation, `1탱 2딜 2힐` slot structure, candidate selection, swap editing, preference-point persistence, and hidden balance-score labels.
`README.md` and `FINAL_OUTPUT.md` are broadly aligned with the implemented sidebar/collapse flow and accurately describe the unrun browser smoke as non-blocking for this round.

findings.title: Saved-player selection does not cover the full visible row body
findings.detail: The spec requires clicking the saved-player row body, including empty space/background, to toggle selection. In the implementation only the inner `#saved-player-toggle-*` button receives the click handler (`src/main.js:90-117`). The wrapper row rendered by `renderSavedPlayer()` is an inert `<article>` containing that button plus a separate delete button (`src/lib/render.js:133-159`). CSS adds visible non-button space to the row via `.saved-player-row { gap: 10px; padding: 6px; }` (`src/styles.css:449-462`), so clicks on the row background/padding/gap do not toggle selection. The test named as full-hit-area coverage only clicks `#saved-player-toggle-*`, so this acceptance criterion is not actually verified (`test/appFlow.test.js:240-269`).
findings.fix: Make the row container itself the selection target for every non-delete area, or restructure the markup so a single control spans the full visible row body except the isolated delete action. Update the automated test to click row-level background space, not only the inner toggle button.

findings.title: The responsive fallback breaks the new compact one-line saved-player rows below 960px
findings.detail: Round 4 prioritizes a compressed one-line saved-player list, but the responsive CSS explicitly turns rows back into stacked vertical layouts at narrower widths: `.saved-player-row` switches to `flex-direction: column` and `.saved-player-row-button` switches to `grid-template-columns: 1fr` inside `@media (max-width: 960px)` (`src/styles.css:982-1008`). That reintroduces taller rows and extra vertical growth for the saved-player library in common narrow desktop/tablet widths, which conflicts with the spec’s one-line compact-list requirement and the docs’ current one-line UX description.
findings.fix: Keep the saved-player row horizontally compressed with truncation/ellipsis at narrower widths and limit the responsive fallback to stacking the sidebar itself. If a stacked row is intentional, the acceptance/docs need to be narrowed accordingly instead of claiming one-line rows generally.

required_fixes: Make saved-player row selection truly row-wide for all non-delete visible space and add a test that proves background/empty-space clicks toggle selection.
Preserve the compact one-line saved-player row layout at narrower widths, or explicitly narrow the product/docs expectations if that behavior is not intended.
verification_run: `command -v chromium-browser || command -v chromium || command -v google-chrome || command -v google-chrome-stable || command -v chrome`
release_readiness: Not release-ready. The sidebar refactor is close, but the saved-player row interaction and compact-row UX still fall short of this round’s core acceptance requirements.
